6767e64dThe wording rules do not reach footnote labels, and the disagreement remedy prefers the wrong halfhightillandsias.org · openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site/level-2, docs/matrix/level-2-phone.md · 2026-09-06
Claim

The level-2 spec's wording rules govern "a reassuring sentence", "the page" and "the visible sentence", and its "Prose and tooltip disagree" scenario resolves a conflict between the two by correcting the sentence to the footnote's terms or re-anchoring the footnote.

Code / observed behavior

A footnote's label is author-written prose the reader sees on hover and in the rendered list, and the checked build verifies only path, range and quote — never the label. So the one surface the build cannot check is also the one the spec does not govern, and the consequence is live: the verification pass withdrew the false reassurance from the page's prose, which now says secrets are re-registered at every start, while [^5]'s label still tells the reader they are removed and reissued so that an unclean shutdown leaves nothing stale — the invented staleness property this spec's own "Reassurance is bounded by the cited source" forbids. Both remedies in the disagreement scenario treat the footnote as the correct half, so an editor applying it would restore the withdrawn claim into the sentence.

Why it matters

This is the one defect of the eight specs that touches published text: a false reassurance is on the live page today, in the surface the build does not check, and the spec written to prevent exactly that failure leaves the surface ungoverned and then points the remedy at the wrong half. Finding 1e141597 records the same label from the annotation-file angle; this one is about the rule that was supposed to catch it.

Remedy / check

Say once, in this spec, that a footnote's label is page prose bound by every wording and sourcing rule here, as PATH, GREEN and RED text are. Add the third remedy — the label is rewritten to what the cited range states — and order the remedies by which half the pinned source supports rather than by which half is the footnote. Add a scenario: when a claim is withdrawn from a sentence, the label of every footnote attached to it is checked for the same claim.

Evidence
  • openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site/level-2/spec.md#L150-L151 — “A reassuring sentence MUST claim only the outcome its cited range states”
  • openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site/level-2/spec.md#L205-L206 — “the sentence is corrected to the footnote's terms, or the footnote is re-anchored to a source that states the sentence”
  • docs/matrix/level-2-phone.md#L60 — “Internal secrets are removed and reissued at every start, so an unclean shutdown leaves nothing stale”

process · main · cb07e89c411e6c63abb8995928ed9a6da34ddc8c

778a9057The only page build is Python, which the runtime methodology forbids for committed automationhightillandsias.org · scripts/build-matrix.py, scripts/figures.py, scripts/issues.py, skills/update-website/scripts · 2026-09-05
Claim

The runtime methodology, identical at both tags, forbids Python for runtime, harness or repository scripts, allows Rust and POSIX shell that dispatches existing binaries, and requires explicit approval from the operator before an exception is committed or used by recurring automation.

Code / observed behavior

This repository's page generator is 1,185 lines of Python plus 372 more of inline-SVG figures, and the ledger fold the page now renders adds a third file of 392; package.json wires the generator to npm run build; and two committed skill scripts, checked-build.sh and drift-report.sh, invoke it on every run of the update loop. That is recurring automation. The convention is written down in skills/README.md as an inheritance argument rather than an approval, and the rule's own checker resolves the repository root with git rev-parse and so has only ever scanned the runtime repository. No recorded approval was found in either repository.

Why it matters

The site is the project's public argument that it says what is true about itself, and the security level's whole case is that promises are machine-checked. A methodology rule this repository quietly does not follow is something a reader of that page is entitled to know about, and it is a live risk: the day the checker learns about sibling repositories, the build breaks and the page cannot be regenerated. A Rust rewrite is the approved path and is not small — the markdown dialect, seven callout kinds, the footnote parser with its release-override suffix, the checked-build resolver, the ledger fold and the whole template, with byte-identical output as the acceptance test — and a POSIX-shell port is not permitted by the rule's own wording, since it would not be dispatching an existing binary.

Remedy / check

Ask the operator for the explicit exception the rule provides for, and record it beside the build command in docs/matrix/README.md, naming the three files it covers and the condition — no new Python, replacement in Rust when the page generator is next touched substantially.

Evidence

  • package.json#L6 — “"build": "python3 scripts/build-matrix.py",”
  • skills/README.md#L18-L23 — “runtime's methodology forbids Python for its own committed automation, and this”

865e6b30`--publish-local` serves the whole repository, `.git` included, on a route with no auth gate, with none of the hardening flags the spec's builder carrieshightillandsias · crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs, images/web/entrypoint.sh, spec enclave-service-catalog · 2026-09-05
Claim

`openspec/specs/enclave-service-catalog/spec.md#L61-L65` names `build_catalog_service_run_args` as a source of truth for how a catalog service is launched, and `openspec/specs/enclave-network/spec.md#L53` lists it as the enclave attach site for this service.

Code / observed behavior

`build_catalog_service_run_args` (`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L3368-L3394`) is hardened and digest-pinned — `--cap-drop=ALL`, `--security-opt=no-new-privileges`, `--security-opt=label=disable`, `--userns=keep-id`, `--pids-limit=32`, and an image resolved to `entry.digest`. **It has no production caller**: the only reference in the tree is the test at `#L18836`.

The live path is `fn publish_local_service` (`#L16812`), reached from `--publish-local` (`#L1082-L1084`) and from the MCP `publish_local` tool (`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/tray/mod.rs#L1012-L1017`). It builds its own argv at `#L16841-L16853`:

"--detach", "--rm", "--name", <container>, "--hostname", …, "--network", "tillandsias-enclave", "-v", format!("{}:/var/www:ro,Z", worktree.display()), image /* "tillandsias-web", a mutable tag */

No capability drop, no `no-new-privileges`, no `userns`, no pids limit, no digest pin. `worktree` is `host_project_root().join(project_name)` (`#L16836`) — the project's repository root, `.git` and all — and the image serves it with `httpd -f -p 8080 -h /var/www` (`images/web/entrypoint.sh#L17`) with no config file, so no path is excluded. The route is then registered with `new_route.public = true` (`#L16883-L16885`), which `generate_dynamic_caddyfile` renders as a bare `reverse_proxy` with no `forward_auth` gate — the project's own test at `#L18872-L18886` asserts exactly that.

Why it matters

Any forge agent (the MCP tool is in-forge reachable) can publish `http://www.<project>.localhost/`, and from that moment `.git/config`, `.git/objects/**` and any untracked secret in the working tree are served without authentication to everything that can reach the router. The hardened, digest-pinned builder that the two specs point at as the implementation is dead code, so reviewing it tells you nothing about what runs.

Remedy / check

Have `publish_local_service` call `build_catalog_service_run_args` (deleting its inline argv), and give the web image an httpd config that refuses dot-directories — or mount a build output directory rather than the repository root.

Evidence

  • images/web/entrypoint.sh#L17 — “httpd -f -p 8080 -h /var/www”

defect · v56.9.5.1 · b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b

b28aba62No default install path verifies a Cosign bundle, and the Linux installer continues when the checksum file is missinghightillandsias · scripts/install.sh, scripts/install-macos.sh, scripts/install-windows.ps1, spec update-system · 2026-09-05
Claim

`openspec/specs/binary-signing/spec.md#L27-L30` — "All signable release artifacts MUST be signed with Cosign keyless mode and MUST be verifiable locally using the bundle format." Verification itself is placed on the user: `#L45-L52` requires only that the *instructions* and `scripts/verify.sh` use `cosign verify-blob --bundle`.

Code / observed behavior

`cosign` appears in no installer. `scripts/verify.sh` is the only consumer (`#L46`, `#L78`), and it is an opt-in helper the install path never calls. The three install scripts stop at SHA-256: `scripts/install.sh#L226-L239`, `scripts/install-macos.sh#L106-L128`, `scripts/install-windows.ps1#L361-L390`.

`scripts/install.sh` additionally proceeds on every failure of that weaker check — `#L232` "sha256sum not found; skipping checksum verification.", `#L235` "SHA256SUMS did not contain $ASSET; skipping checksum verification.", `#L238` "SHA256SUMS not available; skipping checksum verification." — and then installs the downloaded bytes at `#L243`. (`install-macos.sh` and `install-windows.ps1` do die on a missing manifest; only the Linux path degrades open.)

`openspec/specs/update-system/spec.md` — the spec governing how a running install obtains a new artifact — contains one requirement, "Platform-appropriate artifact selection", and the strings `cosign`, `verify`, `signature` and `checksum` do not appear in it at all.

Why it matters

The signing story the spec tells is only ever exercised by an opt-in helper, so the default path a user actually runs verifies nothing stronger than a checksum — and on Linux not even that, because every failure of the checksum step is a warning followed by an install of the downloaded bytes. The spec that governs how a running install fetches a new artifact does not mention verification at all.

Remedy / check

Make `install.sh` fail closed when `SHA256SUMS` is missing or does not name the asset, and add a signature-verification requirement to `openspec/specs/update-system/spec.md` (verify the bundle when `cosign` is present, refuse or warn loudly when it is not).

Evidence
  • scripts/install.sh#L238 — “SHA256SUMS not available; skipping checksum verification.”
  • openspec/specs/binary-signing/spec.md#L27-L30 — “All signable release artifacts MUST be signed with Cosign keyless mode and MUST be verifiable locally using the bundle format.”
  • openspec/specs/update-system/spec.md#L8-L14 — “The updater SHALL select the correct artifact for the current platform and handle platform-specific execution constraints.”

No upstream issue filed.

defect · v56.9.5.1 · b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b

da34e5eeFive production container launches never reach `validate_launch_argv`, and one of them builds an argv the policy forbidshightillandsias · crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs, crates/tillandsias-podman/src/container_spec.rs · 2026-09-05
Claim

`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L11681-L11688` — "VERIFIED 2026-09-04: this function's only production caller is `run_agent_container_attached`, which validates first; its four other callers are inside `mod tests` … **Every production container launch therefore already passes `validate_launch_argv`.**" A second doc comment at `#L14177` states "Every option flows through the policy-validated `build_run_argv()` path".

Code / observed behavior

`ContainerSpec` has two serializers: `build_run_argv()` validates (`container_spec.rs#L394-L397`), `build_run_args()` does not (`#L274`). These production paths use the unvalidated one, or build argv by hand and hand it straight to `PodmanClient::run_container_observed` (`crates/tillandsias-podman/src/client.rs#L1022`), which performs no validation:

- the egress proxy — `main.rs#L3414` `fn build_proxy_run_args` returns a raw `Vec<String>`, launched at `#L3526`; - the git mirror — `main.rs#L4284` `fn build_git_run_args`, launched at `#L9087`; - the observatorium web container — `main.rs#L11246` `.build_run_args()`; - the project browser — `main.rs#L11295` and `#L13047` `spec.build_run_args()`; - the interactive forge — `build_forge_agent_run_args_with_vault` ends at `#L14736` with `spec.build_run_args()`, and `build_forge_agent_run_argv` (`#L14741`) merely prefixes `podman run` before `launch_forge_agent` (`#L15089`) spawns it in a host terminal emulator. This is the path the `#L14177` doc comment describes, and it never calls the validator.

And the gap is not theoretical. `fn run_provider_login` (`main.rs#L9607`) launches a container at `#L9722-L9740` with `--cap-drop=ALL`, `--security-opt=no-new-privileges` and `--userns=keep-id` — but **not** `--security-opt=label=disable`, which `policy.rs#L17-L22` (`MANDATORY_HARDENING_FLAGS`) declares mandatory. `validate_launch_argv` would return `MissingMandatoryHardening(["--security-opt=label=disable"])` for that argv. Nothing calls it there, so the launch proceeds.

Why it matters

The project's own framing (`container_spec.rs#L385-L392`) is that an argv missing a hardening flag "is not a degraded launch to be reported, it is a container that must not be created". At this tag that guarantee holds for exactly the delegated-agent lanes, while the proxy, the mirror, the observatorium, the browser and the interactive forge — the containers a user actually runs — are outside it, and there is already one production argv the policy would reject.

Remedy / check

Route every builder through `build_run_argv()` (or call `validate_launch_argv` in `run_container_observed` / `run_container_attached_observed` so no launcher can bypass it), fix `run_provider_login`'s missing flag, and correct the two doc comments.

Evidence
  • crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L11684-L11688 — “VERIFIED 2026-09-04: this function's only production caller is `run_agent_container_attached`, which validates first; its four other callers are inside `mod tests` (which begins at the #[cfg(test)] at line 16663, and all four sit past it). Every production container launch therefore already passes `validate_launch_argv`.”
  • crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L9734-L9736 — “"--cap-drop=ALL", "--security-opt=no-new-privileges", "--userns=keep-id",”
  • crates/tillandsias-podman/src/container_spec.rs#L385-L392 — “is not a degraded launch to be reported, it is a container that must not be created”

No upstream issue filed.

spec-vs-code · c4039e1 · c4039e18f5533054f368b9836867655880d55c09

0d88cfc7The level specs restate site/level-common's shared rules instead of referencing themmediumtillandsias.org · openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site · 2026-09-06
Claim

site/level-common exists so that the shared rules are "stated once so the per-level specs can say only what is particular to their page", and each level spec defers to it by name where a rule is shared.

Code / observed behavior

Eight defects across five reviews are one shape: the level spec restates the shared rule rather than referencing it. Level 1 re-asserts level-common's RED lifecycle in a scenario under a requirement that has just deferred to it, and its footnote-past-the-pin scenario is level-common's. Level 2 restates the RED lifecycle and narrows it — a replaced defect "MUST be written in the past tense", where level-common allows a past-tense flag or a GREEN — and then says its lifecycle is as level-common states. The cross-level same-source sentence is verbatim in both level 1 and level 2. The page-furniture ban appears in levels 1, 2, 3 and 4. Level 3 copies level 1's footnote-target sentence verbatim, and reproduces the no-path sentence level-common already carries. Level 5 restates level-common in four requirements (own pin, verdicts re-derived, sourcing, audit annotations), and states the newer-build/@vTAG rule three times inside its own file, a fourth in level-common and a fifth in level-5-stable-pin-deltas.

Why it matters

Normative copies drift independently: an editor correcting one leaves the others contradicting it, and level 2's copy already narrows what level-common permits, so two editors reading two specs reach opposite verdicts on the same fixed RED. Two of the duplicated rules are also cross-level by construction — a level cannot satisfy "cite the same source as the other level" alone — so no level spec is the right owner. Nothing here misleads a reader today: the specs are unpublished and govern no page yet. They are what the next update loop reads.

Remedy / check

Reduce each restating half to a reference to level-common, and move the two genuinely shared rules the level specs invented — levels agree on a source for a shared claim; page furniture lives in the LEVELS table — into site/level-common, so each level spec carries only its particular.

process · main · cb07e89c411e6c63abb8995928ed9a6da34ddc8c

1e3f8c3dThe navigation spec describes a progress board the build does not producemediumtillandsias.org · openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site/navigation, scripts/build-matrix.py · 2026-09-06
Claim

The navigation spec requires the board to place every finding in exactly one of three columns whose blurbs a reader who has never opened the ledger can apply, to show per finding whether it has been filed where it has to go, to show when each was first recorded and last moved, and to order each column by a rule the build states.

Code / observed behavior

Three of those do not hold. The ledger's lateral terminals, obsoleted and wontfix, are not ladder rungs and are placed in the middle column by the fold, but the spec's middle-column blurb requires that a plan of work exists and the left requires found-and-not-yet-tracked, so such a card matches no blurb the page states. The filing state is computed and then discarded: build-matrix.py builds the filed-or-unfiled markup into `up` and appends it behind a literal `if False`, and would emit it as a sibling list item outside the card even if the guard were flipped, so no card on the published board carries a filing link or says "not filed upstream". A finding whose events carry no timestamp renders as a blank meta field rather than as explicitly undated, and the ordering rule (severity, then id) exists only as a Python sort key.

Why it matters

The requirement the board exists for — an unfiled finding MUST NOT be displayed in a way that lets it read as filed — is unmet by omission for every runtime finding on the live board, mitigated only by the aggregate "0 filed upstream" tally beside it. The column defect is in the opposite direction: the spec is unpublished and the fold already does something defensible, but the blurb a reader is told to apply and the placement the code performs disagree, so the first wontfix will be misfiled by the page's own definition.

Remedy / check

In the build, drop the `if False` and emit the filing state inside the card. In the spec, name where a lateral terminal sits in the ledger's own terms — on the board, never in the right-hand column, its card saying the attempt ended without completion — widen the middle column's stated meaning to cover it, require a finding with no chronology to render as undated rather than blank, and say where the ordering rule is stated.

2448903cThe startup context says on-demand installs verify a Sigstore attestation; the shim disables attestation, and the Homebrew prefix is backed by no volumemediumtillandsias · images/default/lib-common.sh, images/default/brew-shim-exec.sh, images/default/Containerfile · 2026-09-05
Claim

The same file repeats it in the shim-generation comment at `#L3336`: "(homebrew-core formulae only, Sigstore attestation verification REQUIRED)".

Code / observed behavior

`images/default/brew-shim-exec.sh#L89` — `export HOMEBREW_NO_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS=1`, with a long, correct explanation at `#L62-L88` of why it had to be turned off (the attestation path calls `gh attestation verify`, which needs a GitHub credential the forge deliberately does not have) and what replaced it (Homebrew's own signed formula index, which the comment is careful to call "authenticated integrity from a single publisher … NOT provenance").

Separately, the prefix that install lands in is `BREW_PREFIX="${TILLANDSIAS_BREW_PREFIX:-/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew}"` (`brew-shim-exec.sh#L32`). `/home/linuxbrew` exists only as a directory created in the image (`images/default/Containerfile#L27`); no builder mounts a volume there. The per-project tool-cache volume mounts `/home/forge/.cache/tillandsias-project` (`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L14414-L14416`), a different path. Forge containers run `--rm` (`ContainerSpec::new` sets `remove: true`, `crates/tillandsias-podman/src/container_spec.rs#L121`), so the Homebrew clone and every installed bottle are discarded when the container exits and re-fetched on the next launch.

Why it matters

The startup context is the security story an agent is given about the tools it installs, and it asserts a provenance check that the shim explicitly turns off — the one place where the code comment is more honest than the user-facing text. The unbacked prefix is a second, quieter cost: an "on-demand install" that is redone from scratch every launch, against an egress allowlist, rather than cached.

Remedy / check

Rewrite both lib-common.sh strings to describe what actually holds (signed formula index → bottle checksum; no attestation, no provenance), and mount a named volume at `/home/linuxbrew` in the forge builders.

Evidence
  • images/default/lib-common.sh#L4515-L4517 — “That install is NOT free — it verifies a Sigstore attestation per bottle and is time-bounded, so it can fail with "this tool is unavailable".”
  • images/default/brew-shim-exec.sh#L89 — “export HOMEBREW_NO_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS=1”
  • images/default/brew-shim-exec.sh#L32 — “BREW_PREFIX="${TILLANDSIAS_BREW_PREFIX:-/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew}"”

No upstream issue filed.

Ten of forty-four footnotes is close to a quarter of the page, and the level-5 rule forbids doing that work as an ordinary edit: each is a delta with evidence and a verbatim quote at the target tag, in a change the operator reviews. Written down now, at the tags where both sides were read, the next pin bump is mechanical; discovered at bump time it is a re-derivation of the strong-law argument under time pressure.

Put the six-row drift table and the four suffix footnotes into the next level-5 change's tasks.md as its work list, with [^16] flagged as needing new prose rather than a new anchor.

The Linux lane discovers what to sign and then proves the property over whatever was staged: `.github/workflows/release.yml#L264-L268` loops `for artifact in *` (skipping only `SHA256SUMS` and existing bundles), and `#L293` runs `bash ../scripts/check-release-asset-integrity.sh .`, whose own header (`scripts/check-release-asset-integrity.sh#L14-L20`) exists precisely because "the Windows job's signing loop was an ALLOW-LIST".

The operator asked for the capability inventory, and an inventory is a completeness claim: it is worth having because it enumerates, and cannot be halved without becoming a sample. One requirement in the level-common spec stating the argument/reference split — levels 1 and 2 stay readable in one sitting, levels 3 to 5 are as long as their subject provided every section earns its place under the rules that already exist — so the next editor is bound by a written rule.

3ed0ddf7Requirement text carries dated findings, counts and rosters that level-common forbidsmediumtillandsias.org · openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site/level-{2,3,4},navigation · 2026-09-06
Claim

The shared contract forbids a page spec's requirement text from carrying a dated finding, a file count or a mandated verdict on a specific flag, and says such findings are work items in the change's tasks.md while the spec states the property the finding is an instance of.

Code / observed behavior

Four specs do exactly what that requirement forbids. Level 4's "RED precision and scope" hard-codes three audit findings — a litmus corpus count down to the literal replacement phrase, a "(server-side branch protection)" scope that the page has already stopped using, and a mandated verdict on one named footnote — all three already tracked as work items in this change's own tasks.md. Level 3's survivorship requirement hard-codes a roster of artifacts two requirements after the same spec rejects prose rosters on principle, and the roster does not match the page: the host working copy it names appears on the page only inside a RED. Level 2 counts today's sources and headings into MUST text ("the two honest limits", "the page's four questions"). The navigation spec conditions a MUST NOT on a dated measurement of the runtime's local-ci.sh — a weight table over CI check names — which the review found half-superseded at the newest daily, where the arithmetic is run by a score-checks subcommand.

Why it matters

A requirement that names an instance duplicates the ledger and rots against it: it mandates a false number the moment the philosophy adds a limit, the page answers a fifth question or the litmus corpus grows, and the navigation clause is unappliable because the progress page has no pin and the answer differs by release. These are the specs' own stated rule being broken by the specs, not a claim to a reader: nothing is published, so no reader is misled today.

Remedy / check

Reduce each to the durable property it is an instance of — a number in prose is re-derived at the pin or replaced by the unquantified noun; a claim about state outside the repository is scoped to what the repository evidences; the page states what survives for every artifact whose fate it asserts — and leave the instances in tasks.md and the dated audit record.

467f07baThe proxy CA is one persistent RSA-2048 30-day certificate; the spec promises a per-launch two-level EC P-256 chain on tmpfsmediumtillandsias · spec proxy-container, crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs, images/default/ca-path.txt · 2026-09-05
Claim

`openspec/specs/proxy-container/spec.md#L66` — "The system SHALL generate a fresh two-level CA chain on every proxy launch. The chain SHALL consist of a self-signed Root CA and an Intermediate CA signed by the root, both using EC P-256 keys. All key material SHALL be stored on tmpfs (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tillandsias/proxy-certs/`) and SHALL be destroyed when the session ends (logout/reboot). No CA keys SHALL persist to disk." The four-file table below it names `root.crt`, `intermediate.crt`, `intermediate.key`, `ca-chain.crt`, each with lifetime "Session (tmpfs)", and a scenario requires generation "in under 10ms (EC P-256 key generation)". The spec's Status is `active` with no stale or superseded marker.

Code / observed behavior

`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L3170-L3189` (`fn ensure_ca_bundle`) shells out to `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 … -days 30 -nodes -subj "/C=US/ST=Privacy/L=Local/O=Tillandsias/CN=Tillandsias CA"` — one self-signed RSA-2048 certificate valid 30 days, not a two-level EC P-256 chain. It is not per-launch: `ca_bundle_needs_refresh` (`#L3055-L3068`) returns false while both files are under 25 days old, so a launch reuses the existing key. And it is deliberately not on tmpfs: the directory comes from `tillandsias_core::ca_path::ca_dir()`, whose single-source manifest `images/default/ca-path.txt` declares `${HOME}/.local/state/tillandsias` and explains at length that a durable location was chosen by measurement because "/tmp works everywhere and is the bug" — a reboot on a volatile path made the proxy permanently unrestartable (order 975-rsgm).

Why it matters

The code is right and the spec is wrong, which is the worse direction: the spec is the artifact a reader (or an auditing agent, or this site) treats as the contract, and it currently promises ephemerality that the implementation deliberately abandoned for a documented reason. "No CA keys SHALL persist to disk" is a security claim, and the CA private key persists to `$HOME/.local/state/tillandsias/ca/intermediate.key` for up to 25 days.

Remedy / check

Rewrite the "Ephemeral CA chain (per-launch generation)" requirement to describe the durable single-certificate design and its 25-day refresh, citing `images/default/ca-path.txt` for why the path is not tmpfs.

Evidence

defect · v56.9.21.1 · 2f5f2a90a7b43ecdee766e38561b8e5790c603aa

56435d54`browser.open` cannot resolve a browser binary: the on-demand chromium installer has no consumer, and the chromium images are built but never runmediumtillandsias · crates/tillandsias-browser-mcp/src/launcher.rs, scripts/install-chromium.sh, images/chromium/ · 2026-09-05
Claim

`openspec/litmus-tests/litmus-host-chromium-on-demand-shape.yaml` is green, and its name asserts that host chromium is installed on demand.

Code / observed behavior

`crates/tillandsias-browser-mcp/src/launcher.rs#L67-L91` (`fn resolve_browser_binary`) accepts an explicit override, then `TILLANDSIAS_BROWSER_BIN`, then `TILLANDSIAS_CHROMIUM_BIN`, then looks only under the cache root (`~/.cache/tillandsias/chromium/current/chrome` and four siblings) and otherwise returns `LaunchError::BrowserUnavailable` — declared at `#L21` as "bundled chromium not yet downloaded". There is no `PATH` fallback to a system chrome/chromium.

The only thing that would populate that directory is `scripts/install-chromium.sh`, and nothing invokes it. Outside the script itself, a repository-wide search for `install-chromium.sh` returns no caller anywhere under `crates/`, `scripts/` or `images/`; the only reference that runs is `openspec/litmus-tests/litmus-host-chromium-on-demand-shape.yaml`, whose steps (`#L33-L75`) are `grep` assertions over the script's own text. The shape test is green while the installer has no caller. (The repository already knows: `plan/index.yaml#L22893` carries a packet titled "scripts/install-chromium.sh has ZERO consumers … wire it or tombstone it", so check that packet's state before filing.)

Separately, `images/chromium/Containerfile.core` and `Containerfile.framework` are wired into the build (`scripts/build-image.sh#L214-L215`, `crates/tillandsias-core/src/image_builder.rs#L329-L330`), but no Rust code launches either image — the only non-build references under `crates/` are build plumbing and status maps.

Why it matters

On a fresh host the whole host-browser MCP surface fails at its first call with an error that names a download step no code performs, and the litmus that is supposed to cover "host chromium on demand" cannot detect that because it only greps the installer's source. Meanwhile two multi-hundred-megabyte container images are built on every image pass and never started.

Remedy / check

Call `scripts/install-chromium.sh` from `resolve_browser_binary`'s miss path (or from the tray's first `browser.open`), add a `PATH` fallback for a system chromium, and add one step to the litmus that asserts a *caller* exists rather than only the script's text.

Claim

The level-5 delta discipline says an editor may apply the deltas a change lists, and that the operator reviews the change before it is archived. The record of the work says the remaining deltas are waiting on the operator.

The seven applied deltas D1-D7 are live: eleven of the thirteen task boxes in openspec/changes/level-5-stable-pin-deltas/tasks.md are [x], and the two that are not are the proposed deltas D8 and D9, which the same file says wait for the operator rather than for an editor. Applying before approval is permitted, so this is an unclosed loop rather than a violation. The longer the change sits, the more the next audit's deltas pile onto an unreviewed base.

The operator reviews level-5-stable-pin-deltas and archives it, together with add-level-page-specs, whose task 3.3 names the same sync, so that openspec/specs/site/level-{common,1..5}/ become the current contract and changes/ holds only what is genuinely proposed.

5e3a98f3The enclave-network spec's cleanup-on-exit and lifecycle-telemetry requirements have no implementationmediumtillandsias · spec enclave-network, crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs · 2026-09-05
Claim

`openspec/specs/enclave-network/spec.md#L31-L34` — "**WHEN** the Tillandsias application exits **AND** no containers are attached … **THEN** the system MUST remove the network with `podman network rm tillandsias-enclave`". Code / observed behavior

`graceful_shutdown_async` at `crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L16652` stops `tillandsias-`-prefixed containers and never touches a network. The only `network rm` in the crate is `#L8845`, inside `run_reset_guest` — the explicit `--reset-guest` wipe, not an exit path. `PodmanClient::remove_network` (`crates/tillandsias-podman/src/client.rs#L975`) has no production caller: the only references are `crates/tillandsias-podman-cli/src/lib.rs#L479` (the scenario tool) and a `let _ =` liveness reference at `client.rs#L3374`. The two mandated log strings — `Network created` and `Container attached` — do not appear anywhere under `crates/`, `scripts/` or `images/`.

Why it matters

Two of the four scenarios under the spec's primary requirement, and both scenarios of its telemetry requirement, describe behaviour that does not exist. The network persists across every exit, which is also what makes the `--internal` installed-base gap permanent rather than self-healing, and the `--log-enclave` accountability window the spec promises is empty for enclave lifecycle events.

Remedy / check

Either implement the exit-time `podman network rm` (guarded on zero attached containers) and the two log lines, or mark both requirements `deferred` with the reason, so the spec stops asserting them.

5f323a37The Windows tray reads the secure-wire variable directly, the single-reader ratchet has two slots of slack, and the WSL guest unit never receives the flagmediumtillandsias · crates/tillandsias-windows-tray/src/hvsocket.rs, scripts/check-secure-wire-single-reader.sh, crates/tillandsias-vm-layer/src/wsl.rs · 2026-09-05
Claim

`scripts/check-secure-wire-single-reader.sh#L3-L5` — "`TILLANDSIAS_SECURE_CONTROL_WIRE` has ONE reader, and this ratchets the number of files that name it down, never up." `#L39` sets `BASELINE="${TILLANDSIAS_SECURE_WIRE_READER_BASELINE:-3}"`, and `#L37-L38` says "Lower this as each is converted; it must never rise. 0 means the flip may land."

Code / observed behavior

At this tag exactly one file outside the owning module still reads the variable — `crates/tillandsias-windows-tray/src/hvsocket.rs#L29`, `if std::env::var("TILLANDSIAS_SECURE_CONTROL_WIRE").as_deref() == Ok("on")`, i.e. the case-sensitive byte comparison the guard's own header (`#L15-L20`) identifies as the behaviour that made `On` silently plaintext. So the count is 1 against a baseline of 3: two more direct readers could be added, with two more private interpretations of the value, and the guard would still print `ok`.

The other half is that the flag never reaches the Windows-side server. `crates/tillandsias-vm-layer/src/vz.rs#L859` injects `Environment=TILLANDSIAS_SECURE_CONTROL_WIRE=__SECURE_CONTROL_WIRE__` into the macOS guest's systemd unit; the WSL equivalent, `fn headless_unit` (`crates/tillandsias-vm-layer/src/wsl.rs#L90-L110`), writes only `Environment=HOME=/root` and `Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/0`. The guest headless therefore always runs with the variable unset, so even a tray told `on` would hand a Noise handshake to a server that is not expecting one — which is precisely the one-sided flip the guard's header records as having already happened once (`#L23-L27`, flipped at e6a80609f, reverted at 08a7d3cc7).

Worth recording alongside: the PSK root is `release_root_secret()` (`crates/tillandsias-secure-channel/src/lib.rs#L86-L101`), which on debug builds is the literal `b"tillandsias-dev-root-not-a-secret"` (`#L68`) and on release builds is the SHA-256 of the shipped binary. Both are values an attacker holding a public artifact can compute, so the channel provides version binding, not confidentiality against anyone who has the release. The source comments say this plainly; the word "secret" in the function name does not.

Why it matters

A ratchet with slack is not a ratchet: the guard prints `ok` while two more private readers of the flag may still be added. And the flip the whole mechanism exists to make safe cannot succeed today, because the WSL guest unit never carries the variable, so a tray told `on` would speak Noise at a server that is not.

Remedy / check

Lower `BASELINE` to 1 now (it can only be lowered honestly if it tracks reality), convert `hvsocket.rs` to `tillandsias_control_wire::secure_wire_mode`, and add the `TILLANDSIAS_SECURE_CONTROL_WIRE` line to `wsl.rs`'s `headless_unit` before the default is flipped.

Evidence
  • scripts/check-secure-wire-single-reader.sh#L39 — “BASELINE="${TILLANDSIAS_SECURE_WIRE_READER_BASELINE:-3}"”
  • crates/tillandsias-windows-tray/src/hvsocket.rs#L29 — “if std::env::var("TILLANDSIAS_SECURE_CONTROL_WIRE").as_deref() == Ok("on")”
  • crates/tillandsias-vm-layer/src/wsl.rs#L90-L110 — “Environment=HOME=/root\n\ Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/0\n\”

No upstream issue filed.

Claim

The level-5 spec states its own governing principle — this spec requires the form of the verdicts and never a particular verdict — and level-common orders that a RED the new pin's code has fixed becomes a past-tense flag or a GREEN.

Code / observed behavior

Three requirements do the opposite, and the reviews show two of them already falsified one release forward. Level 4 makes a REFUTED permanent and unconditional, with no pin condition, while the page's only REFUTED says the hardening litmus cannot fail at this release — a claim the change's own tasks.md 4.16 records as no longer holding on the newer build. Level 5's section enumeration mandates today's conclusions rather than the object each section covers: item 4 requires the gap between what the repository asserts of the operator and what the theorem needs, item 6 requires the law-of-large-numbers family the doctrine invokes and the hypothesis the architecture violates by design; the review found both falsified at the only candidate pin, where the workspace property-tests monotonicity of refine and the methodology withdraws its strong-LLN claim. Level 1 requires the method section to carry an honest limit that exists only because the pinned methodology currently withholds a metric proof.

Why it matters

At the next pin bump each of these compels the page to keep a sentence its source no longer supports — the precise failure level-common's RED lifecycle exists to prevent — or leaves the page unable to comply without inventing a defect. The level-5 case also reverses this change's own completed task 2.6, which stripped mandated verdicts out of every requirement. Nothing is published, so no reader is misled today; the cost falls on the first editor to move a pin.

Remedy / check

Condition each on the pin, as level 5's "Verdicts are re-derived, never frozen" already does: name the section's object and the job it does and let the conclusion be a fact of the pin; keep a REFUTED while it holds at the pin and restate it in the past tense, naming the release that changed it, when the pin moves; and require the limit the cited methodology records at the pin rather than today's wording of it.

Change the line to `https://vault:8200`.

8dd0e5c5Nine requirements contradict their own scenario or a sibling requirementmediumtillandsias.org · openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site/level-{1,2,3,4,5} · 2026-09-06
Claim

Each of these requirements is written to be applied by an editor who was not present when it was written, and openspec validate passes on all three changes, so nothing structural flags them.

Code / observed behavior

Nine requirements instruct and forbid the same thing. Level 4's required sections open "in this order" and close by permitting the surface sections to be reordered, silently dropping the assurance-last constraint stated two sentences earlier. Level 4 lists the argument markers as optional, with dropping one explicitly not a regression, while "Rejected arguments stay on the page" makes a REFUTED mandatory. Level 4's hardening requirement governs a "hardening section" its own section list never defines. Level 3 makes it a MUST that each subsystem subsection say what falls short at the pin, and its own third scenario says a subsystem with nothing wrong keeps its subsection. Level 3 requires each unanswered item of a multi-item RED to be named in a scoped no-path clause and then makes the scoping optional in the next sentence. Level 5 requires each argument section to end with the flags that judge it while the same requirement declares markers optional and the page's first argument section carries none. Level 1's app-vocabulary requirement asserts the pinned source records a machine check of the promise it has just shown, and its third scenario forbids presenting that check as proof of that promise. Level 2 requires a cost sentence that its own platform requirement would forbid on Linux, and gives no precedence rule where "verbs match what the code does" and "the footnote target carries the claim" pull in opposite directions — the case that produced both rules.

Why it matters

A requirement that contradicts itself cannot be applied: an editor either picks a half and calls it compliance, or reads the whole spec as approximate. Three of these would license deleting true page content, and one would license writing a claim false on a supported platform. Nothing is published, so no reader is misled today; the damage is to the next editor, who is the reader these specs are written for.

Remedy / check

Resolve each pair in favour of the scenario, which is the half derived from the page: state ordering once and positively; carve the required markers out of the optional list by reference; anchor the hardening rule to the boundary section's hardening paragraphs; make the shortcoming clause conditional; say which no-path form governs and when scoping becomes required; make the flag rule a placement rule; reword the app-vocabulary MUST to permit a machine check only when the written promise it enforces is named; and add the missing precedence clause.

ecbe8175Universal MUSTs assert of the pages and of the audit record what is not true of themmediumtillandsias.org · openspec/changes/add-level-page-specs/specs/site/level-{3,4,5} · 2026-09-06
Claim

These requirements are written as descriptions of the pages they govern and of how the project works, in the register of a contract the page already satisfies.

Code / observed behavior

Eight of them are false of their subject on the day they ship. Level 4 states that audits of the page are run against a build newer than the pin; the page's own annotation file is scoped to the pin itself, and the current dated record says it re-verified every claim at the pin. Level 4 requires promise, reason, price and purchase before the flags of every defended surface; the supply-chain heading is followed immediately by its first GREEN with no prose at all. Level 3 defines its required subsections as one per subsystem a launch brings up unconfigured, which by the page's own account excludes two of its eight subsections, and its add-or-remove scenario then licenses deleting them. Level 3's GREEN attribution MUST is broken by five of nine GREENs, and its "any list" MUST catches an illustrative naming of toolchains that nobody thinks is wrong. Level 5's closed section enumeration has no home for the live RED on the methodology's complexity constraint; its superlative ban forbids the theorem statements the page exists to make; and its Verdict rule requires every sentence there to restate an established claim, which the section's closing line does not.

Why it matters

A requirement falsified by its own subject teaches an editor that this spec's MUSTs are approximate — and several of these, applied literally, would have the editor delete true prose or a live RED to comply. The audit-premise sentence is worse than wrong: it reads as licence to distrust an at-the-pin audit, which is the steady state the update loop aims at. The specs are unpublished, so nothing here misleads a reader today.

Remedy / check

Scope each MUST to the case its own scenarios test, and make the audit premise conditional ("where an audit is run against a build newer than the pin"). Bind the Verdict rule to claims rather than sentences, the superlative ban to claims about the tree, the list rule to lists offered as the inventory of a bounded set, and widen level 3's subsection class to any subsystem a session reaches without the reader configuring it.

373585f1The published site cannot be reached from a forge, so no claim about it was verified as served HTMLlowtillandsias.org · docs/audit, and the proxy allowlist in the runtime · 2026-09-05
Claim

The audit verifies what a reader of tillandsias.org sees, and the update loop ends by publishing to it.

Code / observed behavior

The site is not reachable from the forge that builds it: the connection is reset, because the proxy allowlist is baked into the proxy image and the project's own domain reached it only in the daily channel. So every claim in the day's records about what a reader sees rests on the committed var/html/index.html and its rebuild hash, not on served HTML.

Why it matters

The last link in the chain is unverified. A build can be byte-identical to the committed artifact and the served page still differ — a stale cache, a misrouted deployment, a worker that never took the commit — and nothing in this repository would notice. It is also the only claim class the checked build cannot reach, so it will stay unverified until a session outside the stable image looks.

Remedy / check

Until a forge on a release carrying the allowlist entry can fetch the site, have a host session or the operator fetch the published page and compare its hash with the committed artifact, and record the comparison in the run's record beside the rebuild hash.

`openspec/specs/proxy-container/spec.md#L53` — "**THEN** the proxy SHALL deny the request with HTTP 403"; and again at `#L109` — "**AND** all other domains SHALL be denied with HTTP 403". A third scenario (`#L186-L188`) requires that "the proxy response SHALL include the blocked domain name for debugging".

Code / observed behavior

`images/proxy/squid.conf#L137-L141` — `acl strict_deny_acl localport 3128` followed by `deny_info TCP_RESET strict_deny_acl`, with the inline rationale "Send a TCP reset instead of an HTTP 403 error for strictly-denied runtime traffic. This prevents sophisticated tunneling/exfiltration over denied connections."

Why it matters

The behaviours are not interchangeable for a client: a 403 carries a body naming the blocked domain (which a third scenario in the same spec requires), a TCP reset carries nothing. Anyone debugging a blocked domain from inside a forge, or writing a test against the spec, is told to expect a status code that never arrives. The deliberate choice recorded in the config is the right one; the spec has simply not been updated to it.

Remedy / check

Change the two `HTTP 403` scenarios to `TCP_RESET` on port 3128, and either drop or re-scope the "response SHALL include the blocked domain" scenario, which a reset cannot satisfy.

Evidence
  • openspec/specs/proxy-container/spec.md#L53 — “**THEN** the proxy SHALL deny the request with HTTP 403”
  • images/proxy/squid.conf#L137 — “acl strict_deny_acl localport 3128”
  • images/proxy/squid.conf#L138-L139 — “Send a TCP reset instead of an HTTP 403 error for strictly-denied runtime traffic. This prevents sophisticated tunneling/exfiltration over denied connections.”
  • images/proxy/squid.conf#L141 — “deny_info TCP_RESET strict_deny_acl”

No upstream issue filed.

7d737704A footnote referenced more than once emits a duplicate element identifierlowtillandsias.org · scripts/build-matrix.py, var/html/index.html · 2026-09-05
Claim

The generated page gives each footnote reference an identifier so the footnote list can point back at the place in the prose that cited it.

Code / observed behavior

The identifier is built from the level slug and the footnote number alone, and is emitted at every occurrence of the reference, so a footnote cited twice on one page produces the same id twice. Of the 775 ids in the published page, 56 are emitted more than once — 69 duplicate emissions in all, every one of them a footnote back-reference. For example id="rlevel-1-five-5" appears twice in var/html/index.html.

Why it matters

Duplicate ids are invalid HTML, and the back-link they exist for lands on whichever occurrence the browser reaches first, which is not necessarily the one the reader came from. Assistive technology and in-page anchors both rely on ids being unique.

Remedy / check

Number the occurrences — append an occurrence index to the id for the second and later references — and have the footnote list link to the first.

Evidence
  • scripts/build-matrix.py#L283 — “return '<sup class="fnref" id="r%s-%s"><a%s>%s</a></sup>' % (ctx.level, n, attrs, n)”
  • var/html/index.html — “id="rlevel-1-five-5"”

Code / observed behavior

Its path extraction takes the target out of every footnote definition and drops the trailing release override, so a footnote already anchored at the daily channel with an @vTAG suffix is counted as if it were resolved against the level's pin. Those footnotes are unaffected by a pin bump — the checked build resolves them against the release they name — yet they inflate both the changed-file count and the per-level totals the report prints.

The report exists to size the next promotion. An inflated number is the same kind of lie as an inflated claim on the page: it makes the work look larger than it is, and the one thing that makes a pin bump get postponed is the belief that it is large.

Keep the @vTAG suffix when extracting targets, and exclude from the pin-versus-stable diff every footnote that names its own release.

Not a fix but a sequencing decision: automate the pre-push gate, the forecast and the re-anchor helper first, so that when agents do run, the objective failures are already impossible; then fan out one agent per level with a skeptic each, and gate publication on a human reading the diff.

56415013The checked build passed on footnotes whose release had no checkouthightillandsias.org · scripts/build-matrix.py, skills/update-website/scripts/checked-build.sh · 2026-09-05
Claim

The checked build is the gate this repository calls the thing that stops a lie from deploying: it resolves every footnote target against the checkout for the tag that footnote names, and fails on any unresolved target or drifted quote.

Code / observed behavior

With only the stable checkout present the build printed that all checked footnote targets resolved and exited zero while all 38 footnotes naming the daily channel went unopened — ten of them citing one of eight files that do not exist at the stable tag at all. Three causes: the check returned early when a release had no checkout and recorded nothing; the per-level line said "checked at <pin>" whatever it had actually opened; and the wrapper demanded checkouts only for the tags the levels pin, so the daily tag was never required.

Why it matters

The gate was silent about exactly the citations most likely to drift — the ones a PATH line uses to acknowledge a fix that is in the daily channel and not yet promoted. A gate whose green means only that it opened the easy half is worse than no gate, because the publishing step trusts it.

Remedy / check

Make an unchecked target a first-class result, report it per level and in a summary naming each level and release it could not answer for, require a checkout for every release any footnote names, and refuse the push on any unchecked target.

Claim

`openspec/specs/chromium-safe-variant/spec.md#L18-L19` — "Full network isolation inside the enclave, with allowlist enforcement via the proxy only; no host-gateway internet fallback"; and `#L137-L138` — "**THEN** it SHALL connect through the enclave network **AND** all web egress SHALL traverse the proxy/allowlist path".

Code / observed behavior

`run-safe-browser.sh` execs `scripts/run-safe-browser.sh`, which execs `scripts/launch-chromium.sh safe-browser "$URL" 9222 open_safe_window` (`scripts/run-safe-browser.sh#L42`). That script's podman argv is built at `scripts/launch-chromium.sh#L84-L98`, and line 90 reads:

"--network=${TILLANDSIAS_BROWSER_NETWORK:-host}"

Neither wrapper sets `TILLANDSIAS_BROWSER_NETWORK` — the string does not appear in either file — so the documented entry point for the "safe" variant launches the browser in the host network namespace, with direct internet access and no proxy in the path. The surrounding flags (`--cap-drop=ALL`, `--security-opt=no-new-privileges`, `--read-only`, tmpfs mounts) are all correctly applied; only the network default contradicts the spec.

Why it matters

The variant's name and its spec both say the containment is network containment, and that is the one control the default turns off. A user running `./run-safe-browser.sh --url …` gets a hardened-but-unisolated browser while every other property the spec lists is genuinely enforced, which is the hardest kind of gap to notice.

Remedy / check

Default to `tillandsias-enclave` (`:-tillandsias-enclave`) and keep `host` reachable only by explicitly setting `TILLANDSIAS_BROWSER_NETWORK`.

spec-vs-code · v56.9.5.1 · b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b

6cd2f616The permissive proxy port grants unfiltered egress to every enclave member with no source restrictionhightillandsias · images/proxy/squid.conf, spec proxy-container · 2026-09-22
Claim

`openspec/specs/proxy-container/spec.md#L104` — the dual-port table lists port 3129 as "Permissive | All domains allowed", and `#L112-L114`: "**WHEN** a request is sent through port 3129 **THEN** all domains on SSL ports (443, 8443) SHALL be permitted **AND** domain filtering SHALL NOT apply."

Code / observed behavior

`images/proxy/squid.conf#L60` — `http_port 3129 ssl-bump \` with no bind address, so squid listens on `0.0.0.0:3129` on every interface the container has. `#L133-L134` — `http_access allow CONNECT SSL_ports build_port` / `http_access allow build_port`, with `build_port` defined at `#L93` as `acl build_port localport 3129` and no source ACL anywhere in the file. The container is dual-homed: `crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L3425-L3426` passes `--network ENCLAVE_EGRESS_NETS` (= `"tillandsias-enclave,tillandsias-egress"`, `#L1651`), so the listener is reachable from both networks.

Why it matters

Every enclave container is handed `http_proxy=http://proxy:3128` (`main.rs#L1711-L1717`), but nothing prevents any of them from using `http://proxy:3129` instead and reaching the internet with the allowlist skipped entirely. The port's own header comment (`squid.conf#L6-L45`) is careful and honest about the port having no consumer today, and `scripts/check-proxy-permissive-port-routing.sh` pins that honesty — but "no consumer" is a statement about Tillandsias's own code, not about what an agent inside a forge can dial. Filtering that a client can opt out of by changing a port number is not a boundary, and the explanation pages describe the allowlist as one.

Remedy / check

Bind the permissive listener to loopback (`http_port 127.0.0.1:3129 …`) so it is unreachable from the enclave, or add a source ACL restricting it, until a real consumer exists.

Evidence
  • images/proxy/squid.conf#L60 — “http_port 3129 ssl-bump \”
  • images/proxy/squid.conf#L93 — “acl build_port localport 3129”
  • crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L3425-L3426 — “"--network".into(), ENCLAVE_EGRESS_NETS.into(),”

No upstream issue filed.

6e61831eThe mirror relay wires the GitHub credential helper for any `https://` origin, and the helper answers unconditionallyhightillandsias · images/git/relay-refs.sh, images/git/git-credential-tillandsias.sh · 2026-09-22
Claim

`images/git/git-credential-tillandsias.sh#L34-L37` states the assumption the design rests on: "Drain stdin (git sends protocol/host/path). We do not branch on it: this helper is wired per-invocation by the relay for one specific remote, so answering unconditionally is correct".

Code / observed behavior

`images/git/relay-refs.sh#L182-L221` — the credential wiring is inside `case "$REMOTE_URL" in https://*)`, i.e. it triggers for any HTTPS upstream, not for GitHub specifically. `REMOTE_URL` is the project's own `remote.origin.url`, read from the host checkout and passed into the mirror (`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs` `fn read_host_project_origin_url`, `#L3653-L3660`, and the `remote.origin.url` read at `#L3588`). The helper it installs is `images/git/git-credential-tillandsias.sh`, which does not branch on the host git asks about and returns the Vault-held GitHub token (`#L48-L57`) for whatever host that is.

Why it matters

The helper's assumption ("wired for one specific remote") is enforced nowhere: the relay wires it on the basis of the URL *scheme* alone. A project whose `origin` is any non-GitHub HTTPS remote — or a redirect chain ending at one — gets the user's GitHub token offered to that host on the first push through the mirror. The mirror is the privileged component in this design precisely because it holds the credential the forge is denied; the condition that decides when it hands that credential out should be the host, not the scheme.

Remedy / check

Match on the origin host (`https://github.com/*`, plus any explicitly configured enterprise host) rather than `https://*`, and have the helper read `host=` from stdin and refuse anything it does not recognise.

Evidence
  • images/git/relay-refs.sh#L182-L183 — “case "$REMOTE_URL" in https://*)”
  • images/git/relay-refs.sh#L217-L219 — “GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=credential.helper GIT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER="${GIT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER:-/usr/local/bin/git-credential-tillandsias}" GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="$GIT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER"”
  • images/git/git-credential-tillandsias.sh#L34-L37 — “We do not branch on it: this helper is wired per-invocation by the relay for one specific remote, so answering unconditionally is correct and avoids parsing a format we would then have to keep in sync.”

9f823c95Two scripts create the enclave network without --internal, and the new guard cannot see themhightillandsias · scripts/orchestrate-enclave.sh, scripts/run-forge-project.sh, scripts/diagnose-proxy.sh · 2026-09-22
Claim

The enclave is isolated because its network is created with --internal, and a build-gate check now reads the create sites.

Code / observed behavior

scripts/run-forge-project.sh#L116-L119 and scripts/diagnose-proxy.sh#L90-L93 still create tillandsias-enclave with no --internal; scripts/check-enclave-network-internal.sh#L87-L115 checks a restated three-file list rather than discovering create sites, so both pass the gate.

Why it matters

A stack brought up by either script is not isolated, and the guard's green means only that the three files it names were clean. A check whose coverage is a hardcoded set reports the set, not the property.

Remedy / check

Make the guard discover every create site from source rather than restating a file list, and add the flag to both scripts.

Evidence
  • scripts/run-forge-project.sh#L116-L119 — “network create --driver bridge --subnet "$ENCLAVE_SUBNET"”

No upstream issue filed.

spec-vs-code · v56.9.5.1 · b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b

f664ad4aThe inference engine is fetched at first run from an unpinned `latest` release with no integrity check, the specs promise baked models the image does not carry, and the health check tests the runner binaryhightillandsias · images/inference/entrypoint.sh, images/inference/Containerfile, specs inference-container and zen-default-with-ollama-analysis-pool · 2026-09-22
Claim

`openspec/specs/zen-default-with-ollama-analysis-pool/spec.md#L47-L54` — T0 `qwen2.5:0.5b` and T1 `llama3.2:3b` are both marked "Baked", and "T0 and T1 are baked into the inference image at build time so the first attach has a usable analysis model with zero network overhead"; `#L59` repeats it as a scenario outcome. `openspec/specs/inference-container/spec.md#L285` lists "T0 models baked into image" as a gating point (while `#L110` of the same file says they are pulled at startup — the two specs already disagree with each other).

Code / observed behavior

Three separate gaps in one container.

*Unpinned, unverified engine.* `images/inference/entrypoint.sh#L293` — `OLLAMA_URL="https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/latest/download/ollama-linux-${OLLAMA_ARCH}.tar.zst"`. `latest` is a moving target, and the download at `#L309-L312` is followed by `zstd -dc | tar -xf` and `install -m 0755 … "$OLLAMA_BIN"` (`#L345-L348`) with no checksum, no signature and no pinned digest anywhere in the file. The fetch goes through the enclave proxy, which bumps `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` with a certificate the container is configured to trust (`openspec/specs/proxy-container/spec.md#L36-L42`), so TLS is not standing in for provenance here either.

*Promised baked models that are absent.* `images/inference/Containerfile#L70` only runs `mkdir -p /opt/baked-models && chown`; no `COPY` ever puts a model there, so the seeding block at `entrypoint.sh#L399-L406` has nothing to seed from. T1 is absent altogether: `entrypoint.sh#L120` sets `DEFAULT_MODELS="${TILLANDSIAS_DEFAULT_MODELS:-qwen2.5:0.5b}"`, and the comment at `#L114-L115` records that `llama3.2:3b` was replaced. So `llama3.2:3b` is named by both specs and is neither baked nor pulled.

*A health check that cannot see the failure it was written for.* `images/inference/Containerfile#L118-L121` — `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version && test -x /home/ollama/.ollama/models/.tools/lib/ollama/llama-server`. The header above it (`#L100-L117`) explains the live incident it exists for: the container sat at `Up (healthy)` while every `/api/generate` returned HTTP 500. The repair upgrades the probe from "the port is bound" to "the port is bound and a file is executable" — it still never loads a model, so a present-but-broken engine or an empty model cache still reads healthy.

Why it matters

The engine binary is the largest single untrusted input the runtime installs, and it arrives from a mutable URL into a container that then serves every forge on the enclave. The baked-model promise is what the specs offer as the offline/first-attach guarantee, and it is not there. And the health signal that the launcher's readiness gate believes is still a proxy for serving, not serving.

Remedy / check

Pin the ollama release to a version and verify its published checksum before extracting; then either bake T0/T1 (`COPY` into `/opt/baked-models`) or correct both specs to say the models are pulled and drop `llama3.2:3b`; and make the health check issue one tiny `/api/generate` (or `/api/show`) against T0 rather than stat a file.

Evidence
  • images/inference/entrypoint.sh#L293 — “OLLAMA_URL="https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/latest/download/ollama-linux-${OLLAMA_ARCH}.tar.zst"”
  • images/inference/Containerfile#L64-L70 — “Model pulling is deferred to entrypoint at container startup (first run only).”
  • images/inference/Containerfile#L70 — “RUN mkdir -p /opt/baked-models && chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/baked-models”
  • images/inference/Containerfile#L118-L121 — “CMD curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version >/dev/null \ && test -x /home/ollama/.ollama/models/.tools/lib/ollama/llama-server”

No upstream issue filed.

defect · v56.9.5.1 · b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b

0fdb0cb3The browser allowlist cannot open any window for a project whose directory name contains a dotmediumtillandsias · crates/tillandsias-browser-mcp/src/allowlist.rs, crates/tillandsias-headless/src/local_projects.rs · 2026-09-22
Claim

`browser.open` is offered as a working MCP surface for any local project, and the allowlist is the component that decides which host a project may open.

Code / observed behavior

`crates/tillandsias-browser-mcp/src/allowlist.rs#L233-L246` — `validate()` splits the host on `.` and refuses anything that is not exactly three labels:

let labels = split_host_labels(&host); if labels.len() != 3 || labels[2] != "localhost" { return Err(AllowlistDeny::HostShape); } … if host_project_label != project_label { return Err(AllowlistDeny::ProjectMismatch { … }); }

The project label it compares against is the raw directory name. `crates/tillandsias-browser-mcp/src/server.rs#L62-L63` reads it from `TILLANDSIAS_PROJECT`, which the forge builders set to `project_name` (`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/main.rs#L11236`, `#L14437`), and `project_name` comes from `scan_project_root`'s `path.file_name()` (`crates/tillandsias-headless/src/local_projects.rs#L76-L78`) with no dot-substitution — only a leading-dot skip.

Why it matters

For a project directory such as `tillandsias.org`, the label is `tillandsias.org`, so every candidate host is four labels (`web.tillandsias.org.localhost`) and hits `HostShape`; and a three-label host would fail `ProjectMismatch` because `labels[1]` is `tillandsias`. There is no path through `validate()` that succeeds, so `browser.open` is unusable for the whole class of projects named after a domain — a common naming convention, and the one this very site's repository uses.

Remedy / check

Compare the trailing labels against the project label rather than requiring `len() == 3`, or normalise dots to `-` when deriving the label (matching `project_label_from_path` at `main.rs#L11189`, which already does this for container hostnames) and use the same normalised label on both sides.

Evidence
  • crates/tillandsias-browser-mcp/src/allowlist.rs#L233-L246 — “if labels.len() != 3 || labels[2] != "localhost" { return Err(AllowlistDeny::HostShape); }”
  • crates/tillandsias-headless/src/local_projects.rs#L76-L81 — “let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) else { continue; }; if name.starts_with('.') { continue; }”

No upstream issue filed.

  2. 2026-09-22T18:42:55Z · resolved — At stable v56.9.21.1, crates/tillandsias-browser-mcp/src/allowlist.rs#L250-L257 accepts at least three labels, rejoins the middle labels as the project name, and checks exact equality. A dotted project name is no longer rejected by host shape.

defect · v56.9.5.1 · b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b

66b46da4The runtime issue drafts cited annotated-tag object hashes as commitsmediumtillandsias.org · docs/audit/2026-09-05-issues-tillandsias.md, skills/file-findings/SKILL.md · 2026-09-05
Claim

Each section of the runtime issue drafts is meant to be pasted into the runtime's tracker with the commit its evidence was read at, so a reader can follow the citation to the code.

Code / observed behavior

The header and the Tag line of all 22 issue sections carried the hash of the annotated tag object — 77958f55… for v56.9.5.1, 49458e96… for v56.9.2.1 — rather than the commit it points at. Pasted into the tracker each would have cited a hash that resolves to no commit there. The mistake was in the instruction rather than in the transcription: the issue template in the file-findings skill said only "commit …" beside the tag.

Why it matters

A finding relayed to another project is only as good as its citation. A hash that resolves nowhere makes the whole relay unusable, and the template would have reproduced the error in every future run.

Remedy / check

Peel every hash to the commit, and make the template say to peel — git rev-parse <tag>^{commit} — because a bare rev-parse of an annotated tag gives the tag object.

Evidence
  • docs/audit/2026-09-05-issues-tillandsias.md#L16-L18 — “Tag under audit: **v56.9.5.1** (commit `b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b`).”
  • skills/file-findings/SKILL.md#L53-L55 — “a bare `git rev-parse <tag>` gives the tag”
History
  1. 2026-09-05T19:45:00Z · found — Found in the same end-of-day pass over the day's artifacts as the other completeness findings, and recorded in the commit message of 8007f39.
  2. 2026-09-05T19:45:05Z · resolved — Fixed at 8007f39 and verified in the tree at c4039e1 — the header cites the full peeled commits b528680d2b938b09279e31faee981a8f6e370b3b and d6d3e3ed910feb24579304d08ef464a229eae21f, each section's Tag line cites the peeled short hash b528680, no tag-object hash survives anywhere in the file, and the skill's template now says to peel.

defect · c4039e1 · c4039e18f5533054f368b9836867655880d55c09

67b4a3aaThe audit record's own counts went stale before it was publishedmediumtillandsias.org · docs/audit/2026-09-05-v56.9.2.1.md · 2026-09-05
Claim

The run's record carries the per-level tables and the headline totals for the site the run produced.

Code / observed behavior

It was written mid-run and never updated, so it described a site that was never published: 329 footnotes with 317 quoted against 342 and 330 in the tree it claimed to describe, per-level counts of 22, 141 and 93 against 23, 147 and 99, and a level-2 section still counting a verdict the verification pass deleted and a verified claim the same pass withdrew as false.

Why it matters

This record is the artifact a reader consults to learn what the day's work established. Counts that belong to no tree make every other number in it unfalsifiable, and the level-2 error pointed the wrong way — it reported a reassurance that had been withdrawn precisely because it was false in the reassuring direction.

Remedy / check

Re-derive every count at the commit the record describes, name that commit in the record, and say what actually happened to both level-2 flags.

Evidence
  • docs/audit/2026-09-05-v56.9.2.1.md#L7-L11 — “re-derived at that commit, after the verification pass that followed the”
  • docs/audit/2026-09-05-v56.9.2.1.md#L11-L13 — “342 footnotes across the five pages, 330 of them”

changeNix builder toolboxChecklist complete19 checked · 0 open

Container images built with `podman build` have no staleness detection — once cached, they're never rebuilt even when the Containerfile, entrypoint, or opencode config changes. Users must manually `podman rmi` to force a rebuild. This is broken UX.

changeNative secrets storeChecklist complete15 checked · 0 open

Tillandsias currently stores the GitHub OAuth token in plain text at `~/.cache/tillandsias/secrets/gh/hosts.yml`. This file is mounted read-only into forge containers, but on the host it sits unencrypted on disk. Any process running as the user can read it. On a shared machine or compromised host, this is a credential leak.

changeStale secrets cleanupChecklist complete19 checked · 0 open

Unclean tray shutdowns (crashes, forced termination) leave stale podman secrets in the system. On next startup, secret creation fails with "secret name in use", blocking container launches. This requires manual cleanup (`podman secret rm tillandsias-ca-*`) before the tray can function again.

A checked archival task list records work, not proof that every goal-state behavior still works now.

  • ☑ 3.1 Update cheatsheets/utils/tillandsias-secrets-architecture.md
  • ☑ 3.2 Update commit message with @trace references
  • ☑ 4.1 Manual smoke test

changeCosign signingOpen tasks15 checked · 5 open

SHA256 checksums (Phase 1) prove that a downloaded file matches what was uploaded, but they don't prove who uploaded it. If an attacker compromises the GitHub Release assets or performs a MITM attack, they can replace both the binary and its checksum. Users have no way to distinguish a legitimate release from a tampered one.

A checked archival task list records work, not proof that every goal-state behavior still works now.

Task record
  • ☑ 1.1 Add `id-token: write` to the release workflow permissions in `.github/workflows/release.yml` alongside existing `contents: write`

  • ☑ 2.1 Add `sigstore/cosign-installer` action step (SHA-pinned with version comment) to the release/signing job
  • ☑ 2.2 Add a `cosign version` verification step to confirm successful installation
  • ☑ 3.1 Add signing loop in the release job: after artifacts are collected, iterate over each binary and run `cosign sign-blob --yes --oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com --output-signature {artifact}.sig --output-certificate {artifact}.cert {artifact}`
  • ☑ 3.2 Ensure signing uses `--yes` flag for non-interactive mode (no browser prompt in CI)
  • ☑ 3.3 Verify that each signing operation produces both `.sig` and `.cert` files alongside the binary
  • ☑ 3.4 Add failure handling: if any `cosign sign-blob` command fails, the entire job fails (preventing unsigned releases)
  • ☑ 4.1 Update the GitHub Release creation step to include `.sig` and `.cert` files for each artifact alongside the binaries and `SHA256SUMS`
  • ☑ 4.2 Verify the release contains the correct number of assets: 3 binaries + 3 `.sig` + 3 `.cert` + `SHA256SUMS` = 10 files
  • ☑ 5.1 Add a verification command template to the release notes body, automatically populated with the correct artifact names and repository identity for each release

changeRelease pipelineOpen tasks18 checked · 4 open

Tillandsias targets three platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows) and must be distributed as a single download-and-run binary per platform. This is error-prone, time-consuming, and blocks the rele

changeFix container death detectionOpen tasks0 checked · 19 open

Container death is completely invisible. When a `--rm` container dies, the tray never updates because three independent bugs in `events.rs` conspire to suppress all death events. The event stream silently produces zero events, the fallback polling never notices disappearances, and the user sees a permanently "running" ghost entry.

A checked archival task list records work, not proof that every goal-state behavior still works now.

  • ☐ 3.2 After each `podman ps` poll, emit Stopped for containers that vanished

changeSecret rotation tokensOpen tasks0 checked · 32 open

Today, Tillandsias injects GitHub credentials into containers by writing the user's full OAuth token to `~/.cache/tillandsias/secrets/gh/hosts.yml` and bind-mounting it read-only at `/home/forge/.config/gh/`. This token has `repo`, `read:org`, and `gist` scopes -- full read/write access to every repository the user owns, plus organization data.

A checked archival task list records work, not proof that every goal-state behavior still works now.

Task record
  • ☐ 1.1 Create `src-tauri/src/token_file.rs` module with `token_base_dir() -> PathBuf` function. Resolves the tmpfs-backed base directory: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tillandsias/tokens/` on Linux, `$TMPDIR/tillandsias/tokens/` on macOS, `%TEMP%\tillandsias\tokens\` on Windows. Falls back through the chain if earlier options are unavailable.
  • ☐ 1.2 Add `token_file::write(container_name: &str, token: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String>` function. Creates `<base>/<container_name>/` directory with mode 0700. Writes token to `github_token.tmp` with mode 0600. Atomically renames to `github_token`. Returns the full path to the token file. Logs to accountability window.
  • ☐ 1.3 Add `token_file::delete(container_name: &str)` function. Removes the `<base>/<container_name>/` directory and its contents. Best-effort (no error if already gone). Logs to accountability window.
  • ☐ 1.4 Add `token_file::delete_all()` function. Removes the entire `<base>/` directory tree. Called on app exit. Logs count of deleted token files to accountability window.
  • ☐ 1.5 Create `TokenCleanupGuard` struct that holds the base directory path. Implement `Drop` to call `delete_all()`. This ensures cleanup on panic.
  • ☐ 1.6 Add `mod token_file;` declaration to `main.rs`.
  • ☐ 1.7 Add unit tests for `token_file`: write creates file with correct permissions, write is atomic (no partial reads), delete removes file and directory, delete_all removes all, token_base_dir resolves correctly on each platform (use `cfg(test)` overrides).
  • ☐ 2.1 Create `images/default/git-askpass-tillandsias` script file with the GIT_ASKPASS helper contents. Script reads `/run/secrets/github_token` for password, returns `x-access-token` for username. Must be executable (0755), owned by root in the image.

changeUpdate audit loggingOpen tasks18 checked · 4 open

When `--update` runs or the background auto-updater applies a patch, there is no record of what happened. Users and developers have no way to confirm whether an update succeeded, what version was installed, or when the last check occurred. After the process exits, all context is gone. A persistent audit log closes this gap — it's a plain text file that accum

A checked archival task list records work, not proof that every goal-state behavior still works now.

  • ☑ 1.3 Implement `rotate_if_needed()` — if `update.log` exceeds 1 MB, read all lines, keep last 100, rewrite file, append a `[<rfc3339>] LOG ROTATED (kept last 100 entries)` header line

changeGit mirror serviceOpen tasks0 checked · 35 open

Phase 1 introduced the enclave network and proxy. But credentials (GitHub token, hosts.yml) are still mounted directly into forge containers. The git mirror service eliminates this by isolating all git/GitHub operations into a dedicated container that owns the credentials. Forge containers clone from the mirror — they never touch credentials or the remote.

changeFix shell quote env varsOpen tasks4 checked · 2 open

Container launches from the tray fail on macOS 26+ because the `TILLANDSIAS_HOST_OS` env var value contains a space (`macOS 26.4`). When podman args are joined into a shell command string for `open_terminal()`, the space splits the value — podman interprets `26.4` as a separate image name argument and tries to pull `docker.io/library/26.4:latest`.

A checked archival task list records work, not proof that every goal-state behavior still works now.

Every container restart re-downloads every package the agent installs. Maven, Gradle, Flutter pub-cache, yarn, pnpm, and uv don't even have env vars set, so they default to ep

  • ☐ 1.1 In `crates/tillandsias-core/src/container_profile.rs`, add two `MountSource` variants: `SharedCache` and `ProjectCache`. Resolution: `SharedCache` resolves to `~/.cache/tillandsias/forge-shared/nix-store/` (host) → `/nix/store/` (forge) `:ro`. `ProjectCache` resolves to `~/.cache/tillandsias/forge-projects/<project>/` (host) → `/home/forge/.cache/tillandsias-project/` (forge) `:rw`. Project name passed via launch context.

The `cheatsheets-license-tiered` design introduces a `pull-on-demand` cache at `~/.cache/tillandsias/cheatsheets-pulled/<project>/` with a tiered RAMDISK budget (64 MB modest / 128 MB normal / 1024 MB plentiful) that auto-spills to disk past the cap. changeForge build observability and diagnosticsOpen tasks0 checked · 58 open

Forge image builds take 2+ hours due to re-downloading ~6.5GB of packages on every build, with no visibility into which steps are slowest or largest. Developers can't identify optimization opportunities or diagnose failures in the build or runtime. Container health issues surface only after minutes of silent operation, requiring manual inspection.
